title: Max Planck and the origin of quantum theory
summary: On 19 October 1900 Max Planck presented a new radiation law, according to the Max Planck Society. The Nobel Prize site says he solved the problem of blackbody radiation in 1900 by introducing the theory of quanta, in which radiation consists of quanta with energies set by a new fundamental constant, later called Planck's constant. Physics Today says his insight spurred a quantum revolution.

uncertainty.note: Planck presented his radiation law to the German Physical Society on 19 October 1900 and presented its theoretical derivation using energy quanta on 14 December 1900.

as_recorded.value: Max Planck solved this problem in 1900 by introducing the theory of “quanta”, that is, that radiation consists of quanta with specific energies determined by a new fundamental constant
On 19 th October 1900, a revolution in physics begins unnoticed. On this day, Max Planck presents a new radiation law.

importance.justification: The Nobel Prize site credits Planck with solving the blackbody problem through quanta and a new fundamental constant, and Physics Today says his insights on energy quanta spurred a quantum revolution.

related.because: Einstein adopted and expanded Planck's quantum concept in 1905 to explain the photoelectric effect as light quanta (photons).
Lise Meitner studied and worked as Planck's assistant at the University of Berlin.

beats.caption: In Berlin, Max Planck presents his empirical blackbody radiation law to the German Physical Society.
Planck derives the radiation law by proposing that energy is emitted in discrete quanta, inaugurating quantum physics.
